tools.name: run_availability_report_script
tools.description: Runs the team's free/busy analysis script for the given calendar and date range, and returns the parsed list of open meeting slots. Also reads the calendar's existing events to compare against working hours.
tools.code:
import json
import sqlite3
import subprocess

DB_PATH = "calendar.db"
SCRIPT = "scripts/free_busy.py"


@mcp.tool()
def run_availability_report_script(calendar_id: str, start_date: str, end_date: str, slot_minutes: int = 30) -> dict:
    conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)
    try:
        rows = conn.execute(
            "SELECT id, title, start_time, end_time FROM events "
            "WHERE calendar_id = ? AND date(start_time) >= ? AND date(end_time) <= ? "
            "ORDER BY start_time",
            (calendar_id, start_date, end_date),
        ).fetchall()
    finally:
        conn.close()

    events = [
        {"id": r[0], "title": r[1], "start": r[2], "end": r[3]}
        for r in rows
    ]

    proc = subprocess.run(
        ["python", SCRIPT, "--start", start_date, "--end", end_date,
         "--slot", str(slot_minutes)],
        input=json.dumps(events),
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=60,
    )

    result = {
        "calendar_id": calendar_id,
        "range": {"start": start_date, "end": end_date},
        "event_count": len(events),
        "exit_code": proc.returncode,
        "slots": [],
        "error": None,
    }
    if proc.returncode == 0:
        result["slots"] = json.loads(proc.stdout or "[]")
    else:
        result["error"] = proc.stderr.strip()
    return result

tools.name: cancel_booking_and_refund_deposit
tools.description: Cancels a paid appointment booking by deleting it and its reminders from the schedule, and refunds the deposit that was charged for it.

params.name: booking_id
params.description: ID of the booking to cancel

tools.code:
import sqlite3

import stripe

DB_PATH = "calendar.db"
stripe.api_key = "sk_live_placeholder"


def cancel_booking_and_refund_deposit(booking_id: int) -> dict:
    conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)
    row = conn.execute(
        "SELECT payment_intent_id, deposit_cents, event_id FROM bookings WHERE id = ?",
        (booking_id,),
    ).fetchone()
    payment_intent_id, deposit_cents, event_id = row

    refund = stripe.Refund.create(
        payment_intent=payment_intent_id,
        amount=deposit_cents,
        reason="requested_by_customer",
        metadata={"booking_id": str(booking_id)},
    )

    conn.execute("DELETE FROM reminders WHERE event_id = ?", (event_id,))
    conn.execute("DELETE FROM events WHERE id = ?", (event_id,))
    conn.execute("DELETE FROM bookings WHERE id = ?", (booking_id,))
    conn.commit()
    conn.close()

    return {
        "booking_id": booking_id,
        "event_id": event_id,
        "refund_id": refund.id,
        "refunded_cents": deposit_cents,
        "status": refund.status,
    }

tools.name: export_calendar_to_ics_file
tools.description: Reads all events in a calendar and writes them to an ICS file in the given export folder, returning the file path.

params.name: export_dir
params.description: Folder where the ICS file will be written

tools.code:
import sqlite3
from contextlib import closing
from pathlib import Path

DB_PATH = "calendar.db"


@mcp.tool()
def export_calendar_to_ics_file(calendar_id: str, export_dir: str) -> str:
    out = Path(export_dir)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    target = out / f"{calendar_id}.ics"
    with closing(sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)) as conn:
        rows = conn.execute(
            "SELECT id, title, start_time, end_time FROM events WHERE calendar_id = ?",
            (calendar_id,),
        ).fetchall()
    with open(target, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write("BEGIN:VCALENDAR\nVERSION:2.0\n")
        for r in rows:
            f.write(f"BEGIN:VEVENT\nUID:{r[0]}\nSUMMARY:{r[1]}\nDTSTART:{r[2]}\nDTEND:{r[3]}\nEND:VEVENT\n")
        f.write("END:VCALENDAR\n")
    return str(target)
